entries.headline: Lighthouse Gold issues 35 million shares to option a Guyana gold property
entries.dek: The CSE has accepted the property option deal for filing, though transfer of Guyana's mining permits still needs approval from the country's mines regulator.
entries.caption: Dense tropical rainforest along a river in Guyana's interior, terrain typical of the country's small-scale gold mining districts.

sources.title: Lighthouse Gold Closes Mariwa-Sardine Hill Gold Property Acquisition and Announces Termination of Private Placement

unverified_claims: The characterization of the deal as an 'exclusive right to acquire a 100% interest' rather than a completed purchase rests on the release's own wording; the permits transfer only once Guyana's mines regulator approves it, which has not yet happened.
The reason for the private placement's termination is not given by the company and is not independently known.
brief: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) has received Canadian Securities Exchange acceptance for its acquisition of the Mariwa–Sardine Hill–Lower Cuyuni gold property in Guyana's Oko Gold District, under a property option purchase agreement with 1464911 B.C. Ltd. It has paid US$150,000 cash and issued 35,000,000 shares at C$0.185 each, worth C$6,475,000, plus a US$100,000 deposit paid earlier.

The 35,000,000 shares equal about 15.98% of Lighthouse Gold's outstanding shares and carry a resale restriction of at least four months and a day. The company holds the right to acquire a 100% interest, but the permits transfer only once Guyana's mines regulator, the GGMC, approves it.

Separately, Lighthouse Gold said a private placement it announced on October 22 and 23, 2026, has been terminated, with no securities issued and no proceeds received. The release gives no reason for the termination and no replacement financing has been announced.
body: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT), a Canadian gold explorer focused on Guyana, said it has received acceptance from the Canadian Securities Exchange for its acquisition of the Mariwa–Sardine Hill–Lower Cuyuni gold property in the Oko Gold District of Guyana's Cuyuni-Mazaruni region. The deal is a definitive property option purchase agreement with the vendor, 1464911 B.C. Ltd. Lighthouse Gold has now paid US$150,000 cash and issued 35,000,000 common shares at a deemed C$0.185 each, worth C$6,475,000, on top of a US$100,000 deposit paid earlier under the original letter of intent.

The release describes this as an option rather than an outright purchase: Lighthouse Gold 'holds the exclusive right to acquire a 100% interest' in the property, and the company says any transfer of the underlying mining permits on exercise of that option is subject to approval from Guyana's Geology and Mines Commission. The vendor, 1464911 B.C. Ltd., already held 20,000 Lighthouse Gold shares before the deal and now holds 35,020,000, about 15.99% of the company, following what Lighthouse Gold describes as an arm's-length transaction.

The underlying property, Mariwa–Sardine Hill – Lower Cuyuni, sits in the Oko Gold District of Guyana's Cuyuni-Mazaruni region and comprises three medium-scale mining permits covering about 3,240 acres. Each permit was originally granted on November 4, 2015 for a five-year term and has since been renewed by the Guyana Geology and Mines Commission; the release states the permits are currently in good standing. Lighthouse Gold describes the property as being at an early exploration stage, with no established mineral resources or reserves.

The 35,000,000 consideration shares are subject to a resale restriction until the later of four months and one day from issuance, or ten trading days after the company files financial statements reflecting the acquisition's value. Today's announcement follows two earlier releases on the same transaction, dated June 15 and October 20, 2026, as the deal progressed toward the CSE's acceptance for filing.

Separately, Lighthouse Gold said a private placement it announced on October 22 and October 23, 2026, has been terminated. No securities were issued and no proceeds were received under that financing, and the release gives no reason for the termination and discloses no replacement financing plan.

Lighthouse Gold describes itself as a Canadian gold exploration company focused on advancing exploration and mining assets in Guyana. The release names Will Rascan as interim chief executive officer and Geoff Balderson as chief financial officer and a director, and states that the Canadian Securities Exchange and its Regulation Services Provider do not accept responsibility for the release's adequacy or accuracy.

entries.headline: 600,000 Nvidia AI chips sit stranded in Hong Kong as China withholds approval
entries.dek: Beijing has let only small allotments of about 10,000 H200 chips reach each of four major Chinese tech firms, even as unofficial prices for the chips in China triple.
entries.caption: Shipping containers stacked at a quiet port terminal, where high-value cargo often waits for customs clearance before onward shipment.

sources.title: Exclusive-Nvidia chips pile up in Hong Kong as China withholds import approval
Rocket Doctor AI Inc. (CSE: AIDR) quote, +6.45% on about $30,343
Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI) quote, -3.43% on about $152,295
GoGo AI Network Inc. (CSE: GOGO) quote, +0.00% on about $29,263
PERIMETER MEDICAL IMAGING AI IN (TSXV: PINK) quote, +0.00% on about $73,998

unverified_claims: The figure of about 600,000 H200 chips stockpiled in Hong Kong is sourced to unnamed 'people familiar with the matter' cited by Reuters, not to an official disclosure by Nvidia or Chinese authorities.
The claim that Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek and Tencent have each received about 10,000 H200 chips rests on unnamed sources; none of the four companies responded to Reuters.
The claim that Beijing previously capped approvals at fewer than 200,000 chips is reporting Reuters attributes to a July report from a separate outlet, The Information.
brief: About 600,000 of Nvidia's advanced H200 artificial-intelligence chips are stranded in Hong Kong awaiting shipment into mainland China, Reuters reported, as Beijing withholds approval for large-scale imports despite strong demand from Chinese technology firms. Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek and Tencent have each received about 10,000 H200 chips in recent months, according to people familiar with the matter.

The scarcity has pushed up unofficial prices: an eight-card H200 server sold for more than 6 million yuan, or about $900,000, in mainland China by late October, roughly three times its price a year earlier, Reuters reported. Servers built with Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips commanded more than 20 million yuan apiece. Beijing's restraint reflects concern about dependence on US technology.

On the venture boards, the artificial-intelligence theme comprises 29 listed names; 17 traded today, 4 higher and 5 lower, for a median move of +0.00% against +2.48% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Rocket Doctor AI Inc. (CSE: AIDR) rose 6.45% to CAD0.495; its registered name contains "ai".
body: About 600,000 of Nvidia's advanced H200 artificial-intelligence chips are sitting in warehouses in Hong Kong awaiting shipment into mainland China, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, as Beijing withholds approval for large-scale imports despite strong demand from Chinese technology firms. Major Chinese internet companies — Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek and Tencent among them — have each received only about 10,000 H200 chips in recent months, the people said, with additional small quantities reaching the mainland through intermediaries and indirect routes.

US export controls dating to 2022 had previously restricted China's access to Nvidia's most capable AI accelerators, and Beijing has imposed its own constraints on the imports in turn, reflecting concern about dependence on American technology.

Earlier reporting cited by Reuters said Beijing had told companies in July that they could expect approval for fewer than 200,000 H200 chips in total for training AI models, with priority for everyday inference work going to domestically made processors instead. China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the National Development and Reform Commission did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment, nor did Nvidia or the four technology companies named in the report.

The scarcity has pushed unofficial prices sharply higher inside China. An eight-card H200 server was offered for more than 6 million yuan, or about $900,000, in the mainland market by late October — roughly three times its price a year earlier, Reuters reported. Servers built around Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips were commanding more than 20 million yuan apiece in the same unofficial market.

On the TSX Venture and CSE boards, 29 listed venture names make up this bulletin's artificial-intelligence theme. Seventeen of them traded today: four moved higher and five moved lower, for a median move of +0.00% against a +2.48% gain for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Twelve saw no trades at all.

Four of the theme's names were among the largest movers. Rocket Doctor AI Inc. (CSE: AIDR), whose registered name contains "ai," rose 6.45% to C$0.495. Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI), also qualifying on its name, fell 3.43% to C$1.97. GoGo AI Network Inc. (CSE: GOGO) and Perimeter Medical Imaging Ai In (TSXV: PINK), both in the theme for the same reason, were unchanged at C$0.015 and C$0.18 respectively.

The moves and the Hong Kong stockpile report fall on the same trading day. Nothing in Reuters' reporting, or in the companies' own filings, connects the two. Twelve of the theme's 29 listed names did not trade at all today.

entries.headline: Copper One's 19.9 million special warrants convert into shares and warrants
entries.dek: The automatic conversion, completing a September financing, hands holders new common shares plus warrants exercisable at $0.50 for two years.
entries.caption: Copper One's September financing completes on November 6 as its special warrants convert automatically into shares and two-year warrants.

sources.title: Copper One Announces Automatic Conversion of Special Warrants. Prospectus Supplement Available on SEDAR+

brief: Copper One Resources will see 19,889,750 special warrants, issued September 29, 2026, automatically convert into common shares and warrants on November 6, 2026, the company said. The special warrants comprised 12,383,000 non-flow-through and 7,506,750 flow-through warrants; holders need take no action.

The conversion delivers 19,889,750 common shares and 9,944,875 share purchase warrants. Each warrant lets the holder buy one common share at $0.50 for two years from the offering's closing date; the company may accelerate that expiry on 30 days' notice if the shares trade at $1.25 or higher for five straight sessions on the CSE.

A prospectus supplement dated November 3, 2026 qualifies the shares and warrants for distribution in British Columbia, Alberta and Ontario and is available on SEDAR+. Copper One trades on the Canadian Securities Exchange under CEXY, on the US OTC market under CEXYF, and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under IW8.
body: Copper One Resources Corp. (CSE: CEXY; OTC: CEXYF; FSE: IW8) will see 19,889,750 special warrants, issued September 29, 2026, automatically convert into common shares and warrants on November 6, 2026, the company said. The special warrants were issued in two tranches: 12,383,000 non-flow-through special warrants and 7,506,750 flow-through special warrants. Holders do not need to take any action; the conversion happens automatically under the terms of the original offering.

The conversion delivers a combined 19,889,750 common shares along with 9,944,875 share purchase warrants to the former special warrant holders. Each warrant entitles the holder to buy one common share at $0.50 for two years from the offering's closing date. The company may accelerate that two-year expiry on 30 days' notice if Copper One's shares trade at $1.25 or higher for five consecutive trading days on the Canadian Securities Exchange.

A prospectus supplement dated November 3, 2026 was filed to qualify the distribution of the securities underlying the special warrants in British Columbia, Alberta and Ontario, and is available on SEDAR+. It follows a short form base shelf prospectus the company filed in May 2025, as amended in March and October 2026. Copper One trades on the Canadian Securities Exchange under CEXY, on the US over-the-counter market under CEXYF, and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under IW8.

This release does not restate the price or use of proceeds from the original special warrant offering; it covers only the terms of today's automatic conversion and the prospectus supplement that qualifies the resulting shares and warrants for distribution.

entries.headline: CopperCorp plans to raise up to C$3 million and shrink its share count
entries.dek: The explorer's non-brokered placement pairs units and subscription receipts with a one-for-five share consolidation ahead of TSX Venture Exchange approval.
entries.caption: Temperate forest in western Tasmania, Australia, where CopperCorp Resources is exploring for copper, gold and rare earth elements.

sources.title: CopperCorp Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement of up to C$3.0M and Share Consolidation

unverified_claims: Whether company insiders will in fact participate in the placement rests on the company's own statement that insiders 'may participate'; this is not yet confirmed.
brief: CopperCorp Resources, which is exploring for copper, gold and rare earth elements at its AMC project in western Tasmania, Australia, plans a non-brokered private placement of up to C$3.0 million. The raise combines up to 4,444,444 units at $0.1125 each, for up to $500,000, and up to 18,518,519 subscription receipts at $0.135 each, for up to $2.5 million.

Each unit carries one post-consolidation share and one warrant exercisable at $0.18 for 24 months; each subscription receipt converts, once escrow conditions clear, into a unit of one share and half a warrant exercisable at $0.24 for 24 months. The conversion depends on completion of the company's Skyline Project sale. Shares carry the usual four-month-and-a-day hold.

CopperCorp is also consolidating its shares on a one-for-five basis, cutting its roughly 118.96 million shares outstanding to about 23.79 million. The financing and consolidation remain subject to final TSX Venture Exchange approval, and proceeds are earmarked for exploration and drilling at the AMC project and for working capital.
body: CopperCorp Resources Inc. (TSXV: CPER; OTCQB: CPCPF), which is exploring for copper, gold and rare earth elements at its AMC project in western Tasmania, Australia, intends to raise up to C$3.0 million through a non-brokered private placement, the company said.

The offering's first tranche is up to 4,444,444 units priced at $0.1125 each, for gross proceeds of up to $500,000. Each unit is made up of one post-consolidation common share and one share purchase warrant, exercisable at $0.18 for 24 months from the date of issue.

The second tranche is up to 18,518,519 subscription receipts priced at $0.135 each, for gross proceeds of up to $2.5 million. Once escrow release conditions are satisfied, each receipt converts into a unit comprising one post-consolidation common share and one-half of a warrant, exercisable at $0.24 for 24 months. The conversion is contingent on completion of the sale of the company's Skyline Project, among other escrow conditions.

CopperCorp is also proceeding with a share consolidation on a one-for-five basis, reducing its roughly 118.96 million shares outstanding to approximately 23.79 million. Securities issued in the placement will be subject to the usual four-month-and-one-day resale hold. Company insiders may participate, which the company says will be treated as related-party transactions.

Proceeds are earmarked for exploration and drilling at the AMC project and for general corporate and working capital purposes, the company said. The offering and the share consolidation both remain subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, and finder's fees may be paid to eligible arm's-length parties under the exchange's policies. CopperCorp also trades on the OTCQB market in the United States under the symbol CPCPF.

entries.headline: Ukrainian drones set fire to a major Ozon warehouse in Russia
entries.dek: The attack hit Adygeysk for a second time, even as Ozon had already projected $367 million in losses from strikes on 11 of its sites.
entries.caption: A freight yard at dusk, the kind of logistics infrastructure Ukraine's drone campaign has repeatedly targeted inside Russia.

sources.title: Ukrainian drone strike sets fire to hub of e-retailer Ozon in southern Russia
Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE: QESS) quote, +5.66% on about $80,085
KRAKEN ROBOTICS INC (TSXV: PNG) quote, -5.57% on about $4,482,396

unverified_claims: Ozon's $367 million loss projection and its order-cancellation response are the company's own statements, not independently verified.
The absence of reported casualties rests on Ozon's and a regional official's statements as reported; no independent casualty count was available.
brief: A Ukrainian drone strike set fire to a logistics hub operated by Russian e-commerce retailer Ozon in Adygeysk, in southern Russia, on November 4, 2026, the company and a regional official said. Debris also damaged two nearby villages. Ozon said it was not aware of any casualties and that all staff had been evacuated.

It was the second strike on this facility. Ukraine has targeted dozens of warehouses run by Ozon and rival Wildberries since July as part of a campaign against Russia's economy and war effort. Ozon said it would cancel orders it cannot fulfil and temporarily stop accepting deliveries from sellers at the site; its shares fell 0.4%.

On the venture boards, the defence theme's 8 names saw 6 trade today, 2 up and 4 down, a median move of -2.62% against +2.48% for the Venture Composite. Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp (CSE: QESS) rose 5.66% to C$0.28, its name containing "defence"; Kraken Robotics (TSXV: PNG) fell 5.57% to C$3.56, its name. Nothing ties the moves to it.
body: A Ukrainian drone strike set fire to a logistics hub operated by Russian e-commerce retailer Ozon in Adygeysk, in southern Russia, on November 4, 2026, the company and a regional official said. It was the second time this specific facility had been hit. Debris from the strike also damaged two nearby villages, according to reporting on the attack. Ozon said it was not aware of any casualties and that all staff at the site had been evacuated.

The strike is part of a broader Ukrainian campaign that has targeted dozens of warehouses run by Ozon and its rival Wildberries since July, aimed at disrupting Russia's economy and its war effort, according to reporting on the pattern of attacks. Ozon said it would cancel orders it could not fulfil from the Adygeysk site and would temporarily stop accepting deliveries from third-party sellers there while it assesses the damage.

Ahead of this strike, Ozon had already projected 30.1 billion roubles (about $367 million) in losses from drone attacks across 11 of its sites, the company said in a financial results release last week. Ozon's stock fell about 0.4% following the latest attack. The strike came as both sides prepared for peace talks scheduled for November 10 and 11, and followed a Ukrainian strike on a Russian oil refinery and Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure in the preceding days.

On Canada's venture boards, the defence and drones theme comprises eight listed names. Six traded today, two higher and four lower, for a median move of -2.62% against +2.48% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of -5.10 percentage points. The attack on Ozon's logistics hub and these moves fall on the same trading day; nothing in either release ties one to the other.

Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp (CSE: QESS) rose 5.66% to C$0.28 and is in the theme because its registered name contains "defence." Kraken Robotics Inc (TSXV: PNG) fell 5.57% to C$3.56 and is in the theme because its registered name is Kraken Robotics Inc. Both traded today; the group's median move was negative even though these two names moved in opposite directions.
